To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a multi-domain adversarially learned network can improve the performance of a single-domain classifier, and (ii) this approach can be used in a semi-supervised setting to leverage multiple datasets in a single domain learning problem.

i) we derive an upper bound for the average and worst domain risk in multi-domain learning; ii) we introduce a novel loss function to address semi-supervised multi- domain learning and domain adaptation, which we call Multi-Domain Adversarially Regularized Neural Network (MuLANN); iii) we validate MuLANN on three datasets, including a bioimage dataset of cultured cells.

MuLANN, a multi-domain adversarially learned network, improves upon existing methods for multi-domain learning in semi-supervised settings, by leveraging multiple datasets with overlapping and distinct class sets.

learning from multiple datasets with overlapping classes, and we provide a new theoretical framework for this setting.
